_exec_summary.SummaryText:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Section A: Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies

Decatur Utilities (DU) operates the Dry Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) where chlorine is used to disinfect the plant effluent water and sulfur dioxide is used to neutralize the chlorinated water before it is discharged to the Tennessee River. 

DU has in place mandatory annual chlorine and sulfur dioxide response training for all employees who work at the WWTP. Additionally, specific training is required in all aspects of the operation of the chlorine and sulfur dioxide processes for those who operate the processes. Training in maintenance and repair of the chlorine and sulfur dioxide process equipment is conducted with all employees who are required to maintain and repair any part of the system. 

Decatur Utilities has developed a chlorine and sulfur dioxide Emergency Response Program to fulfill the requirements of OSHA Part 1910.38. The Emergency Response Plan is coordinated with the local and state emergency response plan.

Section B:  Stationary Source and Regulated Substances Handled

The Dry Creek WWTP has one stationary source capable of holding twelve (12) 1-ton containers of chlorine as well as one stationary source capable of holding eight (8) 1-ton containers of sulfur dioxide. The covered processes consist of piping and chlorine and sulfur dioxide injection equipment specifically designed for each process.

Section C: Worst Case and Alternative Case Scenarios

Decatur Utilities has completed release scenarios for both Worst Case and Alternative Case releases that are most likely to occur at the Dry Creek WWTP given the Chlorination and Dechlorination processes.  

Additionally, the rate of release and endpoints corresponding to the scenarios were derived from the EPA Risk Management Program Guidance for Offsite Consequence Analysis and the EPA Supplemental Risk Management Program for Wastewater Treatment Plants. 

Worst Case Release Scenario

This scenar

io was modeled as a direct release of chlorine/sulfur dioxide over a 10-minute period, as required by the regulations. It involves the catastrophic failure of a 1-ton container due to impact, corrosion, or construction defect. The entire contents of a full container, 2,000 pounds, are released over a ten-minute period at a rate of 200 pounds per minute. The toxic endpoint was modeled as a 1.3-mile radius in all directions from the point of release. The affected population was estimated at 2,700 for a chlorine release and 2,600 for a sulfur dioxide release utilizing EPAs EJScreen Tool.   

Alternative Case Release Scenario

This scenario assumes the release of chlorine/sulfur dioxide through a 1-inch diameter hole in a 1-ton container. It also assumes that the release will continue until the 1-ton container is completely empty. For the chlorine release, the entire contents of a full container, 2,000 pounds, is released over a 13-minute period at a rate of 150 pounds per minute. The toxic endpoint was modeled as a 0.2-mile radius in all directions from the release point. For the sulfur dioxide release, the entire contents of a full container, 2,000 pounds, is released over a 28-minute period at a rate of 71 pounds per minute. The toxic endpoint was modeled as a 0.2-mile radius in all directions from the release point. The affected population for both alternative case scenarios is estimated at 24 utilizing EPAs EJScreen Tool. 

Five Year Accident History

No accidents involving chlorine or sulfur dioxide have occurred at the WWTP in the past 5 years.  

Section D: Prevention Program Elements

Management System

Decatur Utilities has documented a management system and has assigned overall responsibility for development and implementation of the Risk Management Plan to the Risk Management Plan Manager. The management system clearly delineates accountability and responsibility of specific elements of the program to the appropriate Risk Management Plan Team Member.

Proc

ess Safety Information

Current process safety information is available to all operators of the covered processes and maintenance employees in accordance with CFR 40 Part 68.48. Safety information includes current SDS sheets, maximum intended inventory, safe upper and lower temperatures, pressures, and flows, process equipment and material specifications, safe operating procedures and codes and standards used in the design and construction of the process.

Process Hazard Analysis 	

A Hazard Analysis has been performed for the Program II covered processes. A checklist was used from Exhibits F-26, F-27, and F-28 of the EPA Supplemental Risk Management Program for Wastewater Treatment Plants.  Causes of potential accidental release scenarios were investigated and safeguards put in place to prevent a release.  The process hazard analysis was documented and is updated every five years. 

Operating Procedures  

Process operating procedures were reviewed, documented, and refresher training conducted with all plant operators and maintenance employees. Operating procedures cover all phases of process operations including system startup, temporary operations, emergency shutdown, normal shutdown, and startup following an emergency shutdown. Process limits were reviewed and documented. 

Training 

Chlorine and sulfur dioxide safety training is performed at least once every 3 years. This includes training on the WWTP Risk Management Program, upper and lower process limits for each regulated substance and consequences of deviation from the limits, hazards associated with the regulated substances, processes, and procedures, chlorine and sulfur dioxide leak response, operating procedures for the covered processes and a third-party chlorine safety course. 

Mandatory annual training is conducted on the WWTP Emergency Response Plan, process PPE, and first aid measures for chlorine and sulfur dioxide exposures. Employees involved in maintaining the on-going mechanical integrity of

the processes are trained on the hazards of the processes, how to avoid or correct unsafe conditions and the procedures applicable to the employees job tasks. This training shall be completed prior to the employee performing maintenance tasks on equipment involved in the covered processes.  

Documentation of employee attendance at all training sessions is maintained for a period of not less than 5 years.

Mechanical Integrity   

All process equipment, piping, ventilation system, monorail and hoist, have a documented schedule of inspection, and preventive and periodic maintenance. All maintenance inspection and testing on chlorine and sulfur dioxide process equipment is conducted as per manufacturer's recommendations and is consistent with accepted engineering practices. Any deficiencies identified during such maintenance and inspections are addressed in a safe and prompt manner. 

Compliance Audits

Compliance audits are conducted every 3 years by at least one person knowledgeable in the process. A report on the audit findings is generated following the audit and all deficiencies or recommendations are promptly addressed and the resolution is documented. The two most recent audits are maintained at the facility.

Incident Investigation

Specific Incident Investigation reporting and documentation procedures have been implemented and are followed in response to any incident involving a covered process that did or could have reasonably resulted in a catastrophic release of chlorine or sulfur dioxide. 

The Incident Investigation is conducted as soon as possible but no later than 48 hours following the incident. Following the investigation, a summary report is generated and includes, at a minimum, the following information: date of incident, date the investigation began, description of the incident and any contributing factors, and any corrective action or recommendations resulting from the investigation.      

Section E: Five-year Accident History

An accidental re

lease is defined in part 68.42 Section A as having resulted in deaths, injuries or significant property damage onsite, or known offsite deaths, injuries, evacuations, sheltering in place, property damage, or environmental damage. Decatur Utilities has had no accidental releases within the past five years.

Section F:  Emergency Response Program

Decatur Utilities has in place an Emergency Response Program that is coordinated with both state and local emergency response agencies. Additionally, a specific plan has been developed for chlorine and sulfur dioxide emergencies following OSHA Standard 1910.38. The plan is reviewed, and training is conducted with all plant operators and maintenance employees annually. The plan includes comprehensive procedures for on-site emergencies and is designed to coordinate with the state and local emergency response plan.  

Section G: Planned Changes to Improve Safety

Any changes necessary to improve process safety will be promptly addressed when discovered.
